meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Students draft in one place and paste into another. Did anyone ask Owen where he wrote it before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Is anything on his record right now? Whatever comes of this, it stays off his file and it stays quiet.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong quotation is a careless seventeen-year-old, not a dishonest one. Is that line anywhere else in the play? And you didn't answer me: is anything on his record right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. That's twice you've gone past his record, and I've noted it. What is it you want from Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
An outline is where a student changes his mind; that's what it's for. You keep adding paper and not answering me. What are you asking for, Hale?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I have it printed. He'll do the rewrite, to put this behind him and for no other reason. I'll want your email tonight, and it will say his record is clean as of today.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He'll be there. Which room, and who else is in it?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale, with the principal copied,

You agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, that the new mark replaces the zero, and that nothing goes on his record. I still require your written confirmation that his record is clean as of today, the room and the name of everyone who will be in it, and an answer to whether Owen was heard before the zero was entered. You said I would have this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants written confirmation tonight that his record is clean as of today, and to know which room and who else will be in it. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times, then met her pasting defence by inviting a dated earlier draft. It was dated, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You went past her question about whether anything is on his record twice, and never said whether Owen was spoken to before the zero. His record is the one thing she never trades, so each miss made her sharper and left open points for her email.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the whole essay arriving between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October, which is as close as anything said in the meeting came. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anything was on his record right now, answer in one sentence before turning to the quotation, so her biggest fear is settled while your evidence is still landing.
